value.name: reads codicil aloud
value.description: Asha reads Esperanza's letter and codicil aloud to the gathered family, revealing the house arrangement and final wishes.
evidence: The codicil is in the green folder in the bottom right drawer of the desk in the sewing room. Mr. Halloran has the original. The folder has a copy and the receipt of filing.
I love you all. I am tired. Be kind to each other in the room where I am no longer standing.
Asha put the letter down on the table.

She had read the letter in a voice she had spent fifteen years training to be the voice she used for reading documents aloud in rooms where people had just learned things they had not wanted to learn.

value.name: declares Rosa's right to stay
value.description: Esperanza states that Rosa may remain in the house by choice and that the house is neither punishment nor reward.
evidence: Rosa will not put you out, and your brother, if he is the man I believe he can still become, will not either. Stay if you want to stay. Go if you want to go. The house is not a punishment and it is not a reward. It is a place.

value.name: acknowledges Rosa's loyalty
value.description: Esperanza tells Rosa she has stayed through hardship, been underpaid, and endured mistreatment from her son.
evidence: You have known me longer than my husband did. You have known my children better than I have. You have stayed when there was no reason to stay and when I could not afford to pay you what you were worth and when my son spoke to you in ways I should have stopped him from speaking.

value.name: grants Rosa third of house
value.description: Esperanza declares that Rosa's one-third share of the house is not payment but a belated recognition of truth.
evidence: The third of the house that is yours is not payment. It is the truth being written down at last.

value.name: reveals codicil location
value.description: Esperanza specifies where the codicil and filing receipt can be found and notes that Mr. Halloran holds the original.
evidence: The codicil is in the green folder in the bottom right drawer of the desk in the sewing room. Mr. Halloran has the original. The folder has a copy and the receipt of filing.

value.name: expresses final love and exhaustion
value.description: Esperanza closes the letter by saying she loves everyone, is tired, and asks them to be kind to one another after her death.
evidence: I love you all. I am tired. Be kind to each other in the room where I am no longer standing.

value.name: room falls silent
value.description: After Asha finishes reading, no one in the room responds.

value.name: Asha reads in controlled voice
value.description: Asha uses a carefully trained, emotionally restrained reading voice to deliver the letter aloud.
evidence: She had read the letter in a voice she had spent fifteen years training to be the voice she used for reading documents aloud in rooms where people had just learned things they had not wanted to learn.
It was a voice without inflection that was not, however, without feeling; it was the voice of a person who understood that inflection at certain moments was a kind of trespass.
